description: Registry of product claims: every public statement about what QODIQA does maps to evidence that is checked by `npm run claims:check`. Status vocabulary: PROVEN, PROVEN-CAVEAT, IN-SAMPLE, SIMULATED, NOT-DELIVERED, OWNER-PENDING, RETRACTED. When in doubt the weaker status applies.

claims.claim: The intent of a request is written (write-ahead log, fsync) before the provider is called; at boot, entries left open are closed.
claims.caveat: There is no explicit COMMIT entry yet; a stream open at a crash is closed as STREAM_OUTCOME_UNKNOWN; durability across a sudden power loss is not demonstrated on hardware.

claims.claim: Offline verifiers with no dependency on QODIQA code exist in JavaScript and Python, with published test vectors.
claims.caveat: To rely on a verification independently of the instance, the public keys must come from a source other than that instance.

claims.claim: Adapters exist for Azure OpenAI and AWS Bedrock.
claims.caveat: Verified only with simulated transport; no calls to the real hosted services have been made.

claims.claim: Logs are sanitized automatically (PII, tokens). Automatic redaction of AI prompt content is not available.
claims.caveat: Log sanitization only; no data-loss-prevention on prompts or responses.

claims.claim: Technical features that support GDPR work are present: data-subject requests, lawful basis recording and retention.
claims.caveat: These are technical controls, not a certification or a legal assessment.

claims.claim: The OpenAPI specification is generated from the code and checked in CI; an API reference is available and checked against it.
SDKs for TypeScript, Python, Go and Java are available in the repository; each covers every operation of the API contract through generated descriptor tables, and verifies artifacts offline.
claims.caveat: Not published to any registry. Go and Java implement protocol V1 only. The generated operation layer is verified against the contract, not exercised operation by operation against a live gateway; the sign, verify, chat, generic-call and error-mapping paths were run against an installed gateway.

claims.claim: Kustomize, Helm, Terraform, Docker Compose and systemd deployment assets exist, and backup and restore are documented.
claims.caveat: Kubernetes and the Helm chart were exercised only on local kind clusters in the development profile; the production profile (TLS to PostgreSQL and Redis, a shared keystore volume, NetworkPolicy enforcement) was rendered and validated, not run on a real cluster. Incremental backup and point-in-time recovery are not supported.

claims.claim: A protocol-V2 artifact binds the request's query string and the headers the issuer chose, in addition to the method, path and body; changing any of them makes the request fail with REQUEST_MISMATCH.
claims.caveat: Protocol V2 issuance is off by default (QODIQA_PROTOCOL_V2_ISSUE); V1 artifacts keep binding method, path and body only. A raw + or ; in a bound query is refused (use %20, %2B, %3B).

claims.claim: A decision can come with a signed receipt that anyone can verify offline with the gateway's public transparency keys; the receipt proves the gateway recorded the decision, not that the decision was correct.
claims.caveat: Present only when the audit entry and the transparency leaf are persisted (otherwise absent); streaming responses carry no receipt yet; retrieval by request id works for a bounded window (default one hour).

claims.claim: An operator can revoke a single signed artifact before it is used; a revoked artifact is refused before its nonce is consumed.

With audit schema v8 enabled, every request whose provider executed ends with a COMMIT audit entry written after the response: the exact number of output bytes delivered, the hash of the delivered text and how the delivery ended (complete, client disconnected, timeout, cancelled, error); a stream that stops half-way commits the bytes that did reach the client.
claims.caveat: Audit schema v8 is off by default (owner decision), so no COMMIT is written until it is enabled; a request whose process dies between its DECISION and its COMMIT gets a COMMIT with completionStatus OUTCOME_UNKNOWN and 0 bytes (unknown) written by the next boot, not the true delivery record; a COMMIT refused by the audit store is queued durably.

claims.claim: With two or more co-signing witnesses configured, an audit checkpoint is exported as anchored only when at least two cosignatures verify under the trusted witness keys; each witness keeps its own key and its own append-only log and refuses rollback, equivocation and forks, so one compromised or unreachable witness can neither anchor a checkpoint alone nor make the other cosign a different head.
claims.caveat: The witnesses run as separate processes with their own keys in the tests; whether two witnesses are operated by independent parties is a deployment fact (owner-level, FO.10), not something the software can check. With fewer than two witnesses configured the quorum is one.

claims.claim: Audit history can be exported as a sealed archive without deleting anything: the chain segment up to a signed checkpoint, the checkpoint, a manifest of file hashes and a seal signed by the audit-checkpoint key, marked in an append-only hash-chained index and verifiable offline years later; ENFORCEMENT audit events are never deleted automatically, and removing history from the hot store remains an operator-run command that archives and verifies first.
claims.caveat: The exporter covers the file chain; PostgreSQL-authoritative deployments rely on the database backup and the prune archive; moving archives to cold storage and verifying them on a schedule are operator steps.

evidence.regex: ENFORCEMENT category events are NEVER subject to automated deletion

claims.claim: A local sandbox (`qodiqa dev`) starts a gateway with a simulated AI provider and disposable PostgreSQL and Redis for development.
claims.caveat: Local only. A hosted sandbox is specified (docs/operations/hosted-sandbox-spec.md) but not operated; nothing is offered publicly.

claims.claim: Authority can be delegated from one agent to another as a chain of signed grants that only ever narrow (classes, tools, actions, lifetime, depth), verifiable offline, and revocable.
claims.caveat: Pinned by shared test vectors re-derived by three implementations; revocation and agent state are gateway-side. Modelled in TLA+ within small bounds (docs/formal), not proven.
